preamble: larder: a self-hosted, FLOSS household food system (recipes, weekly dinner planning, shared shopping list; later, pantry estimates driven by receipts). Specs: docs/goals.md, docs/requirements.md, docs/specs/, docs/decisions/. Slices titled "Interview:" collect the owner's decisions and come before the slices that depend on them. Every slice has an "Owner input" section listing what to confirm before starting. Household-specific answers go in the gitignored local/ folder, never in committed files.

note_records.text: **2026-10-12** — Owner answer 1 (config file location): the config file is $LARDER_DATA/larder.toml. LARDER_DATA is required and must be an existing directory.
**2026-10-12** — Owner answer 2 (timezone): timezone is a config key, optional, as an IANA name. When it is unset, larder uses the host's local time.

**2026-10-12** — Owner answer 3 (settings sketch, chosen now): people (name, role, autonomy, email, matrix_id, notify_channel); stores (name, senders); category_order; notify_channels; [secrets] paths (deploy_key, imap_password_file, ntfy_token_file). Secrets are paths only, never read or printed.

**2026-10-12** — Gate VERDICT: PASS (opus reviewer). Settings load from $LARDER_DATA/larder.toml plus scalar LARDER_* overrides, reject unknown keys and LARDER_* vars, resolve the data-dir layout and redact secret paths; 20 tests green, ruff clean. Open lows: an env override skips type-checking the file value it replaces; LARDER_DATA is not resolved to an absolute path.

**2026-10-12** — From the S03 review: reconcile the docs/specs/data-model.md Person row with config.Person from S03 (autonomy L0/L1, email, matrix_id), and decide whether people live in config only or are also mirrored in the DB.

**2026-10-12** — Owner decision 2026-10-12: people live in config (config.Person holds role, autonomy and contacts). The DB person table is a thin mirror (id, name UNIQUE, active) so other tables can FK to a person. Syncing it from config is a later slice; S04 only creates the table. This resolves the S03 review note.

**2026-10-12** — Owner decision 2026-10-12: data access is one module per area (src/larder/<area>_db.py) with plain functions taking a sqlite3.Connection; SQL only in those modules, db.py and migrations; documented in AGENTS.md.
**2026-10-12** — Owner decision 2026-10-12: migrations ship as .sql package data and are loaded through importlib.resources.
**2026-10-12** — Owner decision 2026-10-12: the database is SQLite. The owner considered DuckDB and kept SQLite.

**2026-10-12** — Gate VERDICT: PASS (opus reviewer). connect/transaction/migrate plus 0001_init.sql (15 MVP tables + unit_alias, STRICT, explicit ON DELETE, FK indexes); 50 tests green, ruff clean; data-model.md matches the schema. Open lows: concurrent migrate race (noted on S05); a migration containing COMMIT breaks the no-trace promise, so migrations must not contain BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; a future table-rebuild migration doing DROP TABLE recipe would cascade-delete recipe_meta (ADR 0006). Nits: data-model.md Deletes line says staple.item_id is RESTRICT (it is CASCADE); README.md still calls the data model a draft.
**2026-10-12** — Flask was pinned in S02 (requirements.in/requirements.txt). Owner input 2 and the requirements.txt entry under Files now mean only a re-pin check, if one is needed.

**2026-10-12** — From the S04 review: create_app runs migrate on every worker, but db.migrate reads recorded versions outside the write lock (src/larder/db.py:87), so concurrent startup on a fresh DB can raise 'table already exists'. Re-check the version inside the transaction, or migrate once before workers fork.
**2026-10-12** — **2026-10-12** — Owner decision 1 (CSS): a small handwritten stylesheet, src/larder/web/static/larder.css. No dependency and no vendored CSS file.

**2026-10-12** — **2026-10-12** — Owner decision 2 (Flask): Flask is already pinned from S02 (requirements.in/requirements.txt, flask==3.1.3). No re-pin in this slice; requirements files are unchanged.

**2026-10-12** — **2026-10-12** — Owner decision 3 (proxy trust): trusted_proxies is a top-level larder.toml array of IP addresses or CIDR networks, parsed strictly. Forwarded headers (X-Forwarded-For, -Proto, -Host) are applied only when the direct peer address (REMOTE_ADDR) is in the list. The key is file-only, with no LARDER_* override.

**2026-10-12** — **2026-10-12** — Owner decision 4 (migrate race): fixed in this slice. db.migrate re-checks schema_migrations for each pending version inside its BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and skips a version another connection has already applied.

**2026-10-12** — Gate VERDICT: PASS (opus reviewer). create_app (migrate at startup), /healthz with db_version, 404 on the base layout, security headers on every response, trusted_proxies-gated ProxyFix, python -m larder; migrate race fixed by a re-check under the write lock; 71 tests green, ruff clean. Open lows: IPv4-mapped peers (noted on S28); python -m larder prints a traceback for an OSError from ensure_data_dirs. Nits: no test pins LARDER_TRUSTED_PROXIES as rejected; brand link to / 404s until a home page exists.

items.title: Interview: device pairing and admin bootstrap
items.short_title: Interview: device pairing and admin bootstrap

note_records.text: **2026-10-13** — Owner answers 2026-10-13: bootstrap by log link (single use, replaced on restart) and CLI 'python -m larder pair --person NAME'; pairing by QR (segno, approved) + link, 10 min single use; links printed as path only; cookie 1 year sliding; members get 403 on admin pages; unpaired devices get a friendly 401 page; bootstrap picks an admin from config; startup fails with no admin. Recorded in ADR 0010 and S07.

**2026-10-13** — Decisions: invalid, used or expired pairing links all get one plain 404 page (410 would say which). Pair confirm page: GET never consumes; POST consumes in db.transaction and sets cookie, 303 to /. Admin check runs inside the guard, so members get 403 before the CSRF check. Session key file is created by writing a 0600 temp file and os.link into place (atomic); a key under 32 bytes is a ConfigError. Session cookie class overrides get_cookie_secure to follow request.scheme (ProxyFix aware). pairing_token CHECK: kind=bootstrap or (person_id and expires_at not null). pyproject package-data gains web/templates/*/*.html for admin/devices.html. QR is segno svg_inline with omitsize and white background; no style attributes. Unused bootstrap tokens are also deleted at start once an admin device exists. segno 1.6.6, BSD-3-Clause, pinned in requirements.txt.

**2026-10-13** — Review fixes: a bootstrap link is now dead once an admin device exists, at GET (peek) and at POST (rechecked inside the pairing transaction, consume rolled back); MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH 1 MiB so oversized POSTs to /pair/... get 413; OSError on secrets/session_key becomes a ConfigError naming the path (clean exit 2); ADR 0010 now says tokens are looked up by hash and only CSRF tokens use constant-time compare; the no-bootstrap test now leaves the bootstrap token unused so it covers the delete-on-restart branch.

**2026-10-13** — Gate PASS (opus/medium) after one fix round: M1 dead bootstrap link once an admin device exists (peek + consume with rollback), T1 non-vacuous bootstrap cleanup test, L1 MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH 1 MiB, L2 session_key OSError -> ConfigError, ADR wording. Open lows: 413 uses Flask's default page (no error.html handler); the 1 MiB limit is app-wide and undocumented, raise it for any upload feature; AGENTS.md status line still says 'no features yet'.

**2026-10-13** — From S07 review: the device guard serves 401 for any endpoint not in auth_views._OPEN_ENDPOINTS. Serve the manifest and service worker from static (or add them to that set), and never let the service worker cache the 401 unpaired page.
**2026-10-13** — From S07 review: the admin 403 check is request.blueprint == auth_views.admin. Register new admin pages on that blueprint or extend the guard.

note_records.text: **2026-10-12** — From the S05 review: trusted_proxies matching does not unwrap IPv4-mapped peers. On a dual-stack bind (--host :: or a WSGI server listening on ::) an IPv4 proxy appears as ::ffff:a.b.c.d and does not match an IPv4 entry, so forwarded headers are ignored (fails closed). Unwrap address.ipv4_mapped in larder.web._is_trusted, or document listing the mapped form.

**2026-10-13** — From S07 review: every worker that calls create_app runs ensure_bootstrap. With a multi-worker WSGI server without preload, each worker logs its own /pair link, only the last works, and a respawn replaces a link the admin is about to use. Run create_app once (preload or single worker) or move bootstrap to a pre-start step (src/larder/web/__init__.py create_app).

goals:
- G1: Answer "what's for dinner?" in seconds, from meals the household actually makes.
- G2: One shared shopping list that every household member trusts.
- G3: Reduce waste and duplicate purchases using order data instead of manual logging (Phase 2).
- G4: Near-zero required upkeep; optional taps improve accuracy, none are required.
- G5: Usable by non-technical household members without help.
- G6: Portable: any household can run it with its own stores, sources and network (ADR 0015, 0016).
non_goals:
- NG1: Placing store orders automatically.
- NG2: Nutrition or calorie tracking.
- NG3: Access from the public internet.
- NG4: Multi-household or hosted operation in the MVP (future direction, ADR 0016).
- NG5: Exact, item-by-item inventory tracking.
